title: "Babies decide when to deploy effort -- Hard condition"
output:
  pdf_document: default
  html_document: default

There were 5 trials, but only 3 are reported.

Baby typically trying for 20 second, how many pulls that is?

Does baby learn from adult demonstrations as much as from own attempts? If they do, they pull less hard after each demonstration

Affect is not surprise! But willingness to pull shoudl depend on surprise

## hard condition

Negative affect should increase over the 3 trials in easy condition - 
However, if affect is based on discrepancy between the expected outcome and the actual outcome, then it decreases since
baby learns that the task is impossible for baby

Maybe affect should reflect surprise between adult expected outcome and the actual outcome

Force decreases when we infer that the required force is more than available force


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
source('~/Downloads/UfT_DEVELOPMENT/experimental_setup.R')
```

Overriding model parameters

```{r variables, include=TRUE}
# how much force a child can apply - and is willing to apply
# if the required force is beyond this threshold, less and less force will be applied
motivation_threshold = 8 

# assume baby estimates the number of required attempts to be sufficient 
# to succeed with this probability
threshold_probability_of_success = 0.8 

# difficulty - probability of success in one attempt 
# given by Beta distribution with an uninformative prior
baby_success <- list(a=1, b=1) 
adult_success <- list(a=1, b=1)

surprise_treshold = 1 # changing this has an effect on whether the force 
                      # peaks during the first trial, or later
```

## Trial 1 

Adult succeeds on the 5th attempt, baby sets a prior over task difficulty

```{r trial1_easy_adult, echo = FALSE}

# first time we observe adult, we set prior over baby's difficulty
r = observe_adult(FALSE, adult_success, baby_success)
adult_success = r$a
baby_success = r$b 
r = observe_adult(FALSE, adult_success, baby_success)
adult_success = r$a
baby_success = r$b 
r = observe_adult(FALSE, adult_success, baby_success)
adult_success = r$a
baby_success = r$b 
r = observe_adult(FALSE, adult_success, baby_success)
adult_success = r$a
baby_success = r$b 
r = observe_adult(TRUE, adult_success, baby_success)
adult_success = r$a
baby_success = r$b 
plot_difficulty(difficulty, adult_success)

```


Baby pulls, but fails 

```{r trial1_easy_baby, echo = FALSE}

render_baby_attempt = function(baby_success, baby_outcome = FALSE, nudge_attempts = 0) {
  
  required_attempts = force_required(expectation(baby_success)) 
  force <- motivation_sigmoid(required_attempts, motivation_threshold)*required_attempts
  
  result = data.frame()
  attempt = 0
  i = 1
  surprise = 100 # select an arbitrary large number

  while (  # attempt < force |  
           abs(surprise) > surprise_treshold | 
           nudge_attempts > 0) { 
    
    expected_adult_outcome = prob_of_success(required_attempts, adult_success)
    surprise = quantify_surprise(prob_of_success(force, baby_success), baby_outcome)
    
    baby_success = update_skill(baby_outcome, baby_success) # update baby's belief about own ability to solve this task

    a = affect(expected_adult_outcome, baby_outcome)
    help = request_help(adult_success, baby_success, k_helpseeking_willingness)
    
    result <- rbind(result, data.frame(pull = i, force = force, affect = a, help = help, surprise = surprise))
    attempt = force # attempt+force
     
    required_attempts = force_required(expectation(baby_success)) 
    force <- motivation_sigmoid(required_attempts, motivation_threshold)*required_attempts
    i = i+1
    
    nudge_attempts = nudge_attempts-1
  }

  # plot attempt number against result
  p1 <- ggplot(result, aes(x = pull, y = force)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab("Pull") + ylab("Force") + theme_minimal()
  p2 <- ggplot(result, aes(x = pull, y = affect)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab("Pull") + ylab("Affect") + theme_minimal()
  p3 <- ggplot(result, aes(x = pull, y = help)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab("Pull") + ylab("Help request") + theme_minimal()
  p4 = plot_difficulty(difficulty, baby_success, "Baby")
  p5 = ggplot(result, aes(x = pull, y = surprise)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + xlab("Pull") + ylab("Surprise") + theme_minimal()
  grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, ncol = 3, nrow = 2)
  return(baby_success)
}

baby_success = render_baby_attempt(baby_success)

```
